title: FAR Module 5 · TBS 4

fields.label: 3. Initial Contribution Receivable for Long-Term Pledge
4. Release From Restriction for Scholarship Spending

html:
TASK-BASED SIMULATION

Endowment and Contribution Receivable Analysis

Analyze donor-restricted endowment resources, investment return, and an unconditional long-term pledge.

Scenario

Item 1 — Endowment Gift

A donor contributes $500,000 and requires that the principal be maintained as an endowment.

Item 2 — Investment Return

During the year, the endowment earns:

  • Interest and dividends: $22,000
  • Net investment gain: $18,000

The donor requires the investment return to be used only for scholarships.

Item 3 — Long-Term Pledge

A separate donor makes an unconditional promise to contribute $200,000 three years from now.

The present value of the expected payment is $176,000.

Item 4 — Scholarship Spending

During the year, the NFP uses $25,000 of the endowment investment return for qualifying scholarships, satisfying that portion of the donor restriction.

Required

1. Endowment Contribution With Donor Restrictions
2. Total Investment Return
3. Initial Contribution Receivable for Long-Term Pledge
4. Release From Restriction for Scholarship Spending
5. Remaining Restricted Investment Return
explanation:
Item 1 — Donor-Restricted Endowment

The donor requires the principal to be maintained as an endowment.

Contribution With Donor Restrictions = $500,000

Item 2 — Investment Return

Interest & Dividends $22,000 + Investment Gain $18,000 = $40,000 Total Investment Return

Because the donor restricts the return for scholarships, the return is generally included in net assets with donor restrictions until used for that purpose.

Item 3 — Long-Term Pledge

The promise is unconditional and payable several years in the future.

Initial Contribution Receivable = Present Value = $176,000

Item 4 — Release From Restriction

The NFP spent $25,000 on qualifying scholarships.

Release From Restriction = $25,000

Item 5 — Remaining Restricted Return

Investment Return $40,000 − Release $25,000 = $15,000 Remaining

CPA Takeaway

  • Donor-restricted endowments generally increase net assets with donor restrictions.
  • Investment return classification depends on donor stipulations.
  • Long-term unconditional pledges may require present-value measurement.
  • Spending restricted return for the donor's specified purpose generally creates a release from restriction.
